content:
mira: FYI—I've sketched a migration plan to extract the policy/eval engine out of the inference runtime. goal is to reduce hotpath complexity and make rules evolvable without touching the runtime. thoughts?

jon: I like the idea. biggest worry is the added RPC latency on the hotpath. do we have numbers on p50/p99 for a small policy check? :thinking:

devin: p50 is ~0.6ms locally, p99 ~3.2ms for our current in-proc checks on 8k seq. if we do an RPC hop we'll add ~0.8-1.5ms depending on LB & serialization. still under our 20ms SLO but affects tail.

mira: yep. that's acceptable if we do a smart fallback: keep a small local cache of frequently hit rules (prefix cache) and short-circuit on miss with RPC. aim: most requests never go remote.

sam: quick question — who owns the KV cache after extract? runtime or eval service? owning it in runtime keeps hop zero but duplicates logic. owning it in eval service centralizes rules.

rachel: recommend moving ownership to eval service. single source of truth for rules + simpler rollout. runtime keeps an LRU in-memory prefix cache as cache hint only. cache invalidation via push events.

jon: push events = another surface. how do we ensure consistency during rollout? race on config flips could cause bad decisions.

devin: plan: three-stage rollout. 1) proxy mode — runtime forwards eval calls to new service but still uses in-proc results when present. 2) mirror mode — runtime sends copies of requests to new service for validation while still using old results. 3) cutover — switch to service as source. Also a quick kill switch to flip back.

mira: agreeing on stages. add canary by tenant (10% first) and a traffic shadowing window of 24h. we need a cost estimate for shadowing.

sam: ops: shadowing 24h at 10% of traffic is approx 1.2 GPU-hours for our dev cluster? not exact but we should budget $X. I'll ask finance for the exact commit number.

rachel: telemetry checklist: per-request eval latency, hit-rate on local cache, error rates (timeout, 5xx), decision divergence % vs old engine, and per-tenant regressions for top 10 tenants.

mira: add a regression detector for decision divergence that can auto-toggle the cutover flag if divergence > 0.2% for 1h. safe default: auto-fallback but alert SRE.

jon: what about batching semantics? some clients rely on atomic multi-call semantics in the current in-proc path. we need to preserve semantics or provide clear contract.

devin: we'll expose a batched RPC that takes an array of keys and returns a vector of verdicts. keeps latency similar to single call with better throughput. also add monotonic request-id to help dedupe at eval service.

sam: security: ensure mutual TLS between runtime and eval service; tenant-scoped tokens; audit logs of policy evaluations for compliance. ops can help wire KMS.

mira: agreed. add HMAC on payloads to detect replay during the mirror window.

eng-bot: deploy-bot: staging cluster rollout scheduled Thu 14:00 UTC. ensure feature-flag gate enabled: `eval_extract_proxy` set to `on` for staging-tenants.

rachel: test matrix for staging: unit, integration (fake KV), integration (real KV), load test at 2x normal qps, chaos test (drop 5% of eval RPCs), divergence sim (inject diff rules).

devin: load test note: the new service should autoscale by RPS and also expose a concurrency limiter to avoid saturating downstream data stores. we should cap per-pod concurrency to avoid tail spikes.

jon: runtime-side changes: small adapter layer + local LRU cache + config listener for invalidations + metrics hooks. keep default mem usage < 40MB.

mira: timeline proposal: two-week spike to build eval service skeleton + RPC proto; week for runtime proxy + cache; 1 week staging cutover + validation; 1 week canary + monitor; then production ramp. total ~5 weeks.

sam: we should list rollbacks and cutover playbook in runbook: feature-flag flip, route table revert, cache warmup steps, and step to replay mirror logs to verify decisions.

rachel: also add alert thresholds: divergence >0.1% p1, eval service latency p99 > 10ms p1, error rate >0.5% p1.

mira: action items: @devin spike PR for proto & skeleton by EOD Friday; @jon runtime adapter RFC draft by Monday; @sam cost bucket + runbook draft by Monday; @rachel telemetry dashboard outline by Monday.

devin: on it. I'll post a short design doc in #eng-docs and link here.

jon: will start the RFC. can we pair on the batched proto tomorrow?

mira: yes — let's meet 10am PT.

sam: noted. I'll create the runbook skeleton and add rollback steps.

eng-bot: calendar-bot: meeting created: eval-extract-sync @ 10:00 PT tomorrow.

mira: thanks everyone. low churn expected on runtime API surface; main work is telemetry and safe cutover. :white_check_mark:

jon: one more nit — add a compatibility header `X-Eval-Version` on responses so we can debug divergence history.

rachel: good call. also persist a short decision hash in trace logs for cross-service correlation.

mira: perfect. closing the loop — I'll update the migration doc and tag the RFC with the new plan.

sam: ack.
